close_reason: Extracted parse_received_at_field(entry: &Value) -> Result<Option<UTCDate>, Value> at email.rs:1477, alongside the existing parse_mailbox_ids / parse_keywords_field helpers. Three call sites (Email/set create, Email/import, Email/copy) now share the helper. build_email_from_create's doc comment now cites the helper as the validation point rather than handle_email_set specifically. Behaviour preserved for malformed strings (3 existing integration tests still pass); behaviour tightened for non-string receivedAt (number/object/bool — previously silently substituted now_utc_string(), now invalidProperties per RFC 8620 §1.4). New regression test email_set_create_with_non_string_received_at_rejected locks the new shape.
description:
crate-jmap-mail-server/src/email.rs:1589 build_email_from_create parses 'receivedAt' via 'obj_val.get("receivedAt").and_then(|v| v.as_str()).map(UTCDate::from)'. The function comment at 1578-1580 says 'the caller is responsible for rejecting malformed client-supplied values up-front (see handle_email_set) so this helper only sees either a valid string or no field at all.'

This is the 'implicit invariant in your head' pattern the workspace AGENTS.md flags. The function has exactly one caller today (handle_email_set), but:

1. A future contributor adding a second caller of build_email_from_create (e.g. some refactor that pulls Email/import or Email/copy through this helper) will not see the validation requirement unless they read the doc comment carefully. UTCDate::from is infallible-by-construction (truncates / pads malformed strings) per jmap-types::utc_date, so a malformed value would silently produce a wrong UTCDate that sorts incorrectly.

2. The validation lives in handle_email_set:998-1011 — at the wire boundary that's fine. But Email/import (commit 4c8a76a) and Email/copy (same commit) duplicate the same UTCDate::new_validated->invalidProperties pattern inline at their own call sites because they don't go through build_email_from_create. Three copies of the same validation logic; if one of them adds a missing case (e.g. negative offsets), the others drift.

Two improvements:

a. Add 'debug_assert!(obj_val.get("receivedAt").map_or(true, |v| v.as_str().is_some_and(|s| UTCDate::new_validated(s).is_ok())));' at the top of build_email_from_create. Cheap, catches drift in debug builds, no production cost.

b. Extract the validation to a free helper 'validate_received_at(entry: &Value) -> Result<Option<UTCDate>, BadProp>' shared by all three call sites. Single source of truth.
title: build_email_from_create relies on caller-side validation
